Let me analyze this Dafny program failure.

The program is:
```dafny
method GetEven(a: array<nat>)
requires true;
ensures forall i:int :: 0<=i<a.Length ==> a[i] % 2 == 0
modifies a
{
    var i := 0;
    while i < a.Length
    invariant 0 <= i <= a.Length
    decreases a.Length - i
    {
        if a[i] % 2 != 0
        {
            a[i] := a[i] + 1;
        }
        i := i + 1;
    }
}
```

The loop invariant is only `0 <= i <= a.Length`. This doesn't capture the fact that all elements before index `i` have been made even.

The postcondition requires that ALL elements in the array are even. But the loop invariant doesn't state that elements before `i` are even. So when the loop terminates (when `i == a.Length`), we only know `0 <= a.Length <= a.Length`, which doesn't imply the postcondition.

This is a "bridge" problem - the invariant and loop exit condition don't imply the postcondition. The invariant needs to include the fact that all elements before index `i` are even.

The fix would be to add to the invariant:
`forall j:int :: 0 <= j < i ==> a[j] % 2 == 0`

So the corrected invariant line would be:
`invariant 0 <= i <= a.Length && forall j:int :: 0 <= j < i ==> a[j] % 2 == 0`

Let me check the proof obligations:
- spec_element: invariant (the invariant is insufficient)
- proof_obligation: bridge (the invariant + exit condition don't imply the postcondition)

Wait, let me reconsider. The issue is that the invariant doesn't capture the progress made by the loop. When the loop exits, `i == a.Length`, and the invariant only says `0 <= a.Length <= a.Length`, which is just a tautology. It doesn't say anything about the array contents.

This is a "bridge" issue - the invariant combined with the negation of the loop guard (`!(i < a.Length)`, i.e., `i >= a.Length`) doesn't imply the postcondition.

The repair would be to change the invariant to include the property about elements before i being even.

The corrected line: `invariant 0 <= i <= a.Length && forall j:int :: 0 <= j < i ==> a[j] % 2 == 0`
